q: Name a programming language named after a real person.

answers.l: Named for Ada Lovelace. Its military standard number, MIL-STD-1815, is her birth year.
Named for logician Haskell Curry, who also lent his name to currying.
Named for Blaise Pascal, who built a mechanical calculator as a teenager.
Named for A. K. Erlang, the queueing-theory pioneer. Also, conveniently, ERicsson LANGuage.
Bertrand Meyer named it for Gustave Eiffel, whose tower was finished on time and on budget.
Stephen Wolfram named it after himself. The language of Mathematica.
Holt and Cordy, University of Toronto, 1982. A teaching language named for Alan Turing.
Named partly for Thierry Coquand and his Calculus of Constructions. Renamed Rocq in 2025.
A 1990s logic programming language from Hill and Lloyd, named for Kurt Gödel.
A functional logic language. Haskell Curry, again.
A probabilistic programming language named for Alonzo Church, Turing’s doctoral advisor.
An educational object-oriented language named for Grace Hopper.
Wirth and Weber, 1965. A generalization of ALGOL named for Leonhard Euler.
A high-level assembler for GEC 4000 minicomputers, named for Charles Babbage.

nope.python: Named for Monty Python’s Flying Circus. A troupe, not a person.
nope.julia: Its creators say there is no particular Julia.
nope.rust: Named, at least partly, after a fungus.
nope.agda: Named after a hen in a Swedish song. Close?
nope.lovelace: Right person. The language is called Ada.
nope.hopper: Right person. Try the language named Grace.

traps.q: Name the language whose military standard, MIL-STD-1815, honors its namesake’s birth year.
Name the language named for the logician who also gave his name to currying.
